A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NTK-based spectral clustering work. All 26 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–N, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original clustering experiments, ablations, leakage tests, statistical comparisons and computational timings in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the proposed method's benchmark evaluations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same noun-anchored NTK affinity, log-sum-exp proxy, regularized affinity diffusion objective and updates, followed by spectral clustering.

E1.justification: The classical, challenging, fine-grained and domain-shift clustering coverage is unchanged. The appendix evaluations using OpenCLIP, individual prompts and filtered label names are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding main-text and appendix experiments, including CLIP, TAC variants, SIC, GradNorm, alternative kernels and ensembling variants. The new related-work citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions retain train-split noun filtering and test-split evaluation, the same CLIP backbones, seven prompt templates, ACC/NMI/ARI metrics and fixed hyperparameters. The backbone, ablation and leakage-test protocols also match.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter and backbone ablations, convergence and affinity visualizations, domain-shift tests, RAD alternatives, single-prompt analyses and leakage checks are unchanged. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-run averaging for label-name leakage in Appendix L and retain the same statistical-test description and reporting in Appendix M/Table 11. Run-count, seed and uncertainty-reporting information does not change.

E6.justification: Tables 1–12 and the plotted findings retain the same results. For example, Table 1 reports the proposed method's ACC as 98.3% on STL-10 and 84.9% on ImageNet-Dogs in both versions. Figure 3's resizing does not alter its curves.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and NTK formulation, optimization derivations and convergence proof in Appendices B–E, and complexity analysis in Appendix N are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: coupling visual similarity with textual semantics through NTK affinities and adaptively ensembling affinities through RAD. The claims about performance across 16 benchmarks are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of affinity structure, convergence, robustness and leakage tests are retained. Appendix I still identifies the need to specify the cluster count, and Appendix G retains the same data-bias and real-world applicability cautions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub code link after the abstract and states in the Reproducibility Statement that source code is provided in supplementary materials. v1 instead asserted that the main-text implementation details sufficed for reproduction. Implementation settings, hardware and timing information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 replaces Golikov et al. (2022) with Guo and Ye (2024) in the joint spectral embedding/clustering discussion. Appendix A adds Guo et al. (2021), Fu et al. (2025) and Liao et al. (2026), while removing several downstream-task citations. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited edits add the code pointer, rewrite the Reproducibility Statement and update citations and the arXiv version/date. The section order, appendix structure and substantive narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3's panels are slightly enlarged and repositioned, with unchanged curves, axes and caption. The code icon and reference edits produce small layout and text-flow changes; no figures or tables are added, removed or substantially redesigned.

improvement.justification: The new code link and supplementary-code statement improve reproducibility guidance over v1's assertion that its prose suffices. The Section 5 citation replacement also better matches the topic described. These are limited gains: scientific methods, proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and the supplied PDFs do not establish the linked code's availability or usability.
